body.statement: For every two-sided pathwise-interior \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\), the outcome-score restrictions \(E_P(k\mid Y,J=j,X)=0\) are equivalent, cellwise, to \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  The operator \(N=N_B=I_{K^2}-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) is their pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector, \(b_{f_0}(X)\in\operatorname{range}\{G(X)\}\), and \(Qf_0=N_Bf_0-h^{\mathsf T}G(X)^+b_{f_0}(X)\) is the \(L^2(P)\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\mathcal T^\perp\) for every \(f_0\in L^2(P)\).
body.justification: The theorem eliminates the infinite continuous-outcome nuisance pointwise and leaves only one finite conditional Gram solve.
body.gap: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen use an equal-width outcome partition and nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions for the binary continuous-outcome projection; no located source gives this exact multilevel \(K^{2}\)-cell plus \(2K^{2}\)-Gram representation.
body.consumer: It makes exact efficiency computation feasible without selecting an outcome sieve in the continuous birth-weight application.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \((y,x)\) and represent a function of the observed cells by \(k=(k_{az})\).  Conditional independence gives
\[
E(k\mid Y=y,J=j,X=x)=\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}(x)k_{az}, \tag{21}
\]
so all outcome restrictions are exactly \(B^{\mathsf T}k=0\).  Lemma 3A shows that \(N_B\) is idempotent, has this range, and is self-adjoint for \(\langle u,v\rangle_D=u^{\mathsf T}Dv\).  It is therefore the pointwise \(D\)-orthogonal projector.  Since \(R\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{K^2}\), constants over the cells lie in \(\ker N_B\), so \(N_Bf_0\) has conditional mean zero given \((Y,X)\).

For a measurement coordinate \(r=(j,a)\), Bayes' rule gives
\[
E\{kR_{\cdot j}\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid X\}
=\pi_j E\{k\mathbf 1(A=a)\mid J=j,X\}. \tag{22}
\]
The corresponding identity with \(Z=z\) is identical.  Thus, after (21), the remaining two families of restrictions in Theorem 2 are precisely \(E(kc_r\mid X)=0\).  If \(k=N_Bk\), the \(D\)-self-adjointness of \(N_B\) gives
\[
E(kc_r\mid X)=E\{k(N_Bc_r)\mid X\}=E(kh_r\mid X). \tag{23}
\]

If \(v\in\ker G(X)\), then
\[
0=v^{\mathsf T}Gv=E\{(v^{\mathsf T}h)^2\mid X\},
\]
so \(v^{\mathsf T}h=0\) conditionally and \(v^{\mathsf T}b_{f_0}=0\).  Hence \(b_{f_0}\perp\ker G\), which for symmetric \(G\) is \(b_{f_0}\in\operatorname{range}G\).  Therefore \(GG^+b_{f_0}=b_{f_0}\), and
\[
E\{h(Qf_0)\mid X\}=b_{f_0}-GG^+b_{f_0}=0. \tag{24}
\]
Moreover every coordinate of \(h=N_Bc\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}N_B\), so \(Qf_0\) remains in that range.  Equations (21)--(24) and Theorem 2 show \(Qf_0\in\mathcal T^\perp\).

The two successive removed parts are orthogonal: \((I-N_B)f_0\) is pointwise orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}N_B\), and \(h^{\mathsf T}G^+b_{f_0}\) is the conditional orthogonal projection of \(N_Bf_0\) onto the span of \(h\).  Hence, for every \(k\in\mathcal T^\perp\),
\[
E\{(f_0-Qf_0)k\}=0.
\]
The range characterized by the conditional-zero equations is an intersection of kernels of continuous conditional-expectation operators and is closed.  Thus \(Q\) is the asserted orthogonal projection.  The cell and Gram gaps bound its conditional coefficients and ensure measurability and integrability of the fixed-rank pseudoinverse.
